newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to keep eye on trade surplus - govt spokesman.
newsitem.headline: Japan to keep eye on trade surplus - govt spokesman.

text.p: Japan will keep an eye on its trade surplus, but exports are unlikely to rise so rapidly as to rekindle the trade friction seen in the past, the Japanese government's top spokesman said on Wednesday.
Japan's trade surplus showed a steep rise for the second month in a row in May, more than trebling from a year earlier to 738.27 billion yen, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.

"There is no question that the tempo of decline in the trade surplus has slowed down.... There is a need to keep an eye on whether this trend will remain," Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.
Until recently, the ministry steadfastly maintained that the trade surplus was still basically on a downward path, although it rose for some months earlier this year on a year-on-year basis.

Kajiyama, however, brushed aside concerns that Japan's trade surplus would start to rise at a pace which may cause renewed friction between trade partners such as the United States and denied the need for the government to take immediate action.
"The economy is (like a) living organism...taking political measures to suppress the surplus does not necessarily yield good results," Kajiyama said.
"In a larger context, the slowing of the decline (in the trade surplus) is not so bad for Japan."
